title: Holistic pipeline failure detection: programmatic checks + agent inspector
summary: Architecture analysis for a two-tier health check framework that unifies existing ad-hoc failure detection mechanisms (startup reconciliation, container monitor, wave/review caps) under a common HealthCheck interface and adds new checks for phase output presence, state consistency, and LLM-based semantic health evaluation. The framework uses a HealthCheckRunner that dispatches checks at lifecycle trigger points and escalates from fast Tier 1 programmatic checks to Tier 2 agent inspection when structural checks flag degraded health.

problem_statement.description: Pipeline failure detection consists of three isolated mechanisms that share no common abstraction and cannot detect semantic failures. startup_reconciliation.py detects containers missing after restart. container_monitor.py detects containers that exit/fail at runtime. max_waves/max_review_cycles provide blunt iteration caps. None of these can detect cases where infrastructure looks healthy but agents didn't accomplish meaningful work — the issue-835 post-mortem proved this: reviewers exited cleanly (code 0) but had nothing to review because coder work never reached the remote.
goals: Define a shared HealthCheck protocol with HealthResult (HEALTHY/DEGRADED/FAILED) and Action (CONTINUE/FAIL_PIPELINE/ALERT)
Migrate existing startup reconciliation and container monitor logic to implement the interface without rewriting their internals
Add Tier 1 checks for phase output presence (commits on remote, agent output files, contract fields) and state consistency (orchestrator vs Docker vs contract)
Add Tier 2 agent inspector that uses an LLM to evaluate whether meaningful progress was made
Wire trigger points into multi_agent.py (wave complete), routes/pipelines.py (phase complete, startup), and container_monitor.py (runtime tick)
Surface results through the existing EventBus/SSE system for observability

startup_reconciliation.mechanism: reconcile_stale_containers(store, docker_client) runs once at boot in cli.py:cmd_serve(). Collects live Docker container IDs, compares against persisted RUNNING containers in all pipelines, marks missing ones FAILED.
startup_reconciliation.limitations: One-shot only — runs once at startup, not during runtime

container_monitor.mechanism: ContainerMonitor runs a background thread polling Docker every 10 seconds. Emits ContainerEvent types (STARTED/STOPPED/FAILED/REMOVED). Has _reconcile_container_state() function that scans all RUNNING pipelines on FAILED events, marks containers and agents FAILED, uses optimistic locking.
container_monitor.wiring: cli.py creates singleton, registers pipeline reconciliation handler via create_pipeline_reconciliation_handler(repo_path), starts the monitor thread
container_monitor.limitations: Only detects infrastructure failures (exit code != 0). Cannot detect semantic failures (exit code 0 but no meaningful work)

wave_and_review_caps.mechanism: Blunt iteration caps that prevent infinite loops. max_waves stops wave execution after 5 iterations. max_review_cycles breaks the review cycle loop after 3 rejections.
wave_and_review_caps.limitations: No nuance — treats all cap-hits the same regardless of reason. Cannot distinguish 'legitimate iteration' from 'stuck in a loop'

event_system.mechanism: EventBus with pub/sub, async delivery, event history. EventType enum already includes HEALTH_CHECK (unused). Events flow to SSE clients via sse.py and unified_sse.py.
event_system.relevance: Natural integration point for health check results

state_management.mechanism: Git-backed state store with optimistic locking (version field). Pipeline model tracks phases, containers, agents, decisions. PhaseExecution tracks containers, agents, review cycles, artifacts.
state_management.relevance: Health checks must respect optimistic locking. Read-only checks are safe; only the caller (not the check) should mutate state.

implementation_approaches.name: HealthCheck Protocol + HealthCheckRunner + adapter migration (recommended)
implementation_approaches.description: Define a HealthCheck typing.Protocol with check(context) -> HealthResult. Create a HealthCheckRunner that manages registration, trigger-based dispatch, and Tier 1 -> Tier 2 escalation. Wrap existing reconciliation and container monitor in thin adapter classes. Add new Tier 1 checks and Tier 2 agent inspector as separate implementations. Wire triggers at lifecycle points.
pros: Existing mechanisms preserved unchanged (23 tests remain valid)
Protocol enables structural subtyping — adapters, dataclasses, and functions all work
Tier escalation logic is centralized and auditable
Natural extension point for future checks
Health check results flow through existing EventBus
cons: Introduces a new package (health_checks/) and ~10 new files
Adapter indirection adds a thin layer over existing code
Runner must be threaded to all trigger points

implementation_approaches.name: Rewrite existing mechanisms as HealthCheck implementations
implementation_approaches.description: Rewrite startup_reconciliation.py and container_monitor.py as native HealthCheck implementations. Remove the existing standalone functions and replace all call sites.
pros: Single code path for all health checking
cons: High risk — rewrites 23 passing tests worth of battle-tested code
Container monitor's background thread model doesn't naturally fit a check() method
startup_reconciliation's one-shot pattern conflicts with check() which implies repeatable execution
Large blast radius — all call sites in cli.py, container_monitor.py need updates

implementation_approaches.name: Decorator/registry pattern instead of explicit runner
implementation_approaches.description: Use @health_check(tier=PROGRAMMATIC, triggers=[STARTUP]) decorators on check functions. A module-level registry collects them at import time. A run_checks(trigger) module function dispatches.
cons: Import-time side effects make testing harder
Difficult to configure differently in tests vs production
Module-level state couples check definitions to the registry
Harder to inject dependencies (docker_client, store) without globals

recommended_approach.name: HealthCheck Protocol + HealthCheckRunner + adapter migration
justification: Preserves existing battle-tested code without modification — adapter pattern eliminates rewrite risk
typing.Protocol is the idiomatic Python approach for structural interfaces
Explicit HealthCheckRunner is easily testable with mock checks and provides centralized escalation logic
Matches the issue's proposed design (shared HealthCheck interface, two tiers, trigger-based dispatch)
Natural integration with existing EventBus — HEALTH_CHECK event type was already defined for this purpose

design_decisions.title: HealthCheck as Protocol, not ABC
design_decisions.decision: Use typing.Protocol for the HealthCheck interface
design_decisions.rationale: Protocol enables structural subtyping (duck typing), which lets existing functions be wrapped without inheritance. Both dataclass-based checks and simple function adapters can conform. This is the standard Python pattern for interfaces that don't need shared implementation.

design_decisions.title: Runner pattern over decorator/registry
design_decisions.decision: Use an explicit HealthCheckRunner class with register() and run_checks() methods
design_decisions.rationale: Explicit registration makes checks testable in isolation and avoids import-time side effects. The runner can be configured differently in tests vs production. Centralized trigger dispatch logic is auditable.

design_decisions.title: Preserve existing mechanisms, adapt via wrapper
design_decisions.decision: Keep container_monitor.py and startup_reconciliation.py unchanged. Create thin adapter classes that implement HealthCheck by delegating to existing code.
design_decisions.rationale: Both are well-tested (23 tests combined) and production-proven. Rewriting introduces unnecessary risk for no functional gain. The adapter pattern provides the unified interface without touching working internals.

design_decisions.title: Tier 2 uses direct API calls, not sandbox containers
design_decisions.decision: The agent inspector calls Claude API via the Anthropic Python SDK directly from the orchestrator process
design_decisions.rationale: Spawning a container for health evaluation takes 30+ seconds and creates recursive monitoring problems. Direct API calls are fast (~2-5s), lightweight, and don't require container infrastructure. The orchestrator has API access through the proxy.

design_decisions.title: Three-valued action enum
design_decisions.decision: HealthResult.action uses CONTINUE | FAIL_PIPELINE | ALERT rather than binary pass/fail
design_decisions.rationale: Many failure modes are ambiguous. DEGRADED state allows graduated response: log a warning, escalate to Tier 2, or notify operators — rather than immediately killing the pipeline. ALERT provides an intermediate action for human notification without pipeline failure.

design_decisions.title: Tier 2 gated by Tier 1 DEGRADED at WAVE_COMPLETE, unconditional at PHASE_COMPLETE
design_decisions.decision: Limit Tier 2 to WAVE_COMPLETE (only when Tier 1 flags DEGRADED) and PHASE_COMPLETE (always)
design_decisions.rationale: Each Tier 2 call costs ~$0.02-0.10 and takes 2-5 seconds. Running on every tick is wasteful. The DEGRADED gate at WAVE_COMPLETE acts as a cost-effective escalation mechanism. PHASE_COMPLETE always runs both tiers as a final quality gate.

design_decisions.title: PipelineHealthContext with lazy property evaluation
design_decisions.decision: Context object fetches git log/diff and agent outputs lazily, not eagerly
design_decisions.rationale: Tier 1 checks typically need only in-memory pipeline state and container info. Expensive git operations and file reads should only execute when Tier 2 or specific checks access them.

design_decisions.title: Health check results via EventBus + SSE
design_decisions.decision: Emit results as events through the existing EventBus, flowing automatically to SSE clients and status reporter
design_decisions.rationale: No new transport mechanism needed. The EventBus already has HEALTH_CHECK type. SSE clients get health updates in real-time. Event history provides debugging capability.

design_decisions.title: Tier 2 advisory by default, Tier 1 can enforce
design_decisions.decision: Only Tier 1 checks (phase_output, state_consistency) can return FAIL_PIPELINE action. Tier 2 returns ALERT by default.
design_decisions.rationale: LLM-based evaluation may have false positives. Starting with ALERT for Tier 2 provides observability without risking premature pipeline failures. This can be tuned to FAIL_PIPELINE once confidence grows from production data.

HealthStatus.description: Three-valued health assessment. HEALTHY = no issues. DEGRADED = something looks wrong but not conclusively broken. FAILED = clear failure detected.

Tier.description: Check tier. PROGRAMMATIC = fast deterministic checks. AGENT = LLM-based semantic evaluation.

Trigger.description: Lifecycle event that triggers health check execution.

Action.description: What to do with the result. CONTINUE = no action. FAIL_PIPELINE = mark pipeline FAILED. ALERT = emit event + log warning, potentially notify humans.

lazy_properties.git_log: str — git log --oneline -20 on worktree branch
lazy_properties.git_diff_stat: str — git diff --stat on worktree branch vs base

methods.run_checks(trigger: Trigger, context: Pi: Run checks for trigger (Tier 1 first, escalate to Tier 2 if needed)
methods.run_tier1(trigger: Trigger, context: Pip: Run only Tier 1 checks for trigger

container_liveness.name: container_liveness
container_liveness.description: Adapter wrapping existing ContainerMonitor. At STARTUP, checks persisted RUNNING containers against live Docker. At RUNTIME_TICK, reports containers that transitioned to FAILED since last check.
container_liveness.implementation: Delegates to ContainerMonitor.check_container_health() and startup_reconciliation.reconcile_stale_containers(). Does not duplicate their logic.
container_liveness.healthy: All expected containers running or gracefully exited
container_liveness.degraded: A container exited non-zero but pipeline has other running agents
container_liveness.failed: All agents for current phase are dead

startup_state.name: startup_state
startup_state.description: Adapter wrapping reconcile_stale_containers(). Detects pipelines with missing containers after orchestrator restart.
startup_state.implementation: Calls reconcile_stale_containers() and translates the count into HealthResult.
startup_state.failed: One or more pipelines had missing containers

phase_output.name: phase_output
phase_output.description: NEW check. Verifies completed phase produced expected artifacts based on phase type.
phase_output.implementation: For implement: checks git log for new commits on worktree branch, checks .egg-state/agent-outputs/ for expected files, checks contract tasks for COMPLETE status. For plan: checks for architect-output.json and task_planner-output.json. For refine: checks for refiner-output.json.
phase_output.degraded: Some artifacts missing but agents reported success (issue-835 case)
phase_output.failed: No artifacts produced despite agents reporting success

state_consistency.name: state_consistency
state_consistency.description: NEW check. Cross-references orchestrator state vs Docker reality vs contract.
state_consistency.implementation: For each agent in current phase: verify container status in Docker matches pipeline state. Verify contract task statuses are consistent with agent completion statuses.
state_consistency.degraded: Minor drift (container status stale but agent correctly marked)
state_consistency.failed: Major inconsistency (orchestrator thinks agent RUNNING but container gone)

agent_inspector.name: agent_inspector
agent_inspector.description: LLM-based semantic health evaluation. Evaluates whether agents made meaningful progress toward the phase goal.
context_assembly: Pipeline ID, phase, trigger, issue title/body
Agent output files for completed agents
Contract task statuses and review feedback
agent_inspector.error_handling: On API failure, returns HEALTHY with reason='Tier 2 evaluation unavailable — API error'. Health check infrastructure failure must never block pipeline execution.
agent_inspector.cost: ~$0.02-0.10 per invocation. Only runs when Tier 1 flags DEGRADED (WAVE_COMPLETE) or unconditionally (PHASE_COMPLETE).

STARTUP.description: After existing reconciliation runs, create HealthCheckRunner, register all checks, run STARTUP trigger. Additive — existing reconciliation still runs first.

RUNTIME_TICK.description: After _check_all_containers(), if any state changed, run RUNTIME_TICK via runner. Existing event handlers continue to work.

WAVE_COMPLETE.description: After on_wave_complete callback, run WAVE_COMPLETE checks. If FAIL_PIPELINE returned, break wave loop.
WAVE_COMPLETE.code_pattern: results = runner.run_checks(Trigger.WAVE_COMPLETE, ctx); if any_fail_pipeline(results): break

PHASE_COMPLETE.description: Before advancing to next phase, run PHASE_COMPLETE checks (both tiers). If FAIL_PIPELINE, mark phase failed instead of advancing.
PHASE_COMPLETE.code_pattern: results = runner.run_checks(Trigger.PHASE_COMPLETE, ctx); if any_fail_pipeline(results): mark_failed()

ON_DEMAND.description: GET /api/v1/pipelines/{id}/health runs all checks on demand. New endpoint, no existing code changed.

event_flow.description: Runner emits events through EventBus for each check result. Events flow to SSE clients automatically. Status reporter includes health info.

new_files.purpose: HealthCheck protocol, HealthResult, HealthStatus, Tier, Trigger, Action enums
HealthCheckRunner: registration, trigger dispatch, escalation, event emission
Tests for core types and runner

modified_files.changes: Add HEALTH_CHECK_STARTED, HEALTH_CHECK_COMPLETED, HEALTH_CHECK_DEGRADED, HEALTH_CHECK_FAILED to EventType enum
Add HealthCheckResultModel for persistence. Add optional health_check_results field to PhaseExecution.
Initialize HealthCheckRunner, register all checks, run STARTUP trigger after existing reconciliation
Add optional runner integration for RUNTIME_TICK triggers on state changes
Add WAVE_COMPLETE health check trigger after wave completion, break on FAIL_PIPELINE
Add PHASE_COMPLETE health check trigger before phase advancement
Add GET /api/v1/pipelines/{id}/health on-demand health check endpoint

what_this_catches_in_issue_835.tier1_phase_output: Implement phase completed, but phase_output check finds no new commits on the remote branch and no agent output files with substantive content -> DEGRADED. This alone would have flagged the problem before reviewers were spawned.
what_this_catches_in_issue_835.tier2_agent_inspector: At PHASE_COMPLETE, inspector reads reviewer output files (empty), checks git diff (no changes), evaluates against issue goal -> FAILED with reasoning: 'Reviewers produced no review content. Git diff shows no substantive changes from the implement phase. The coder work likely did not reach the remote branch.' Suggested action: ALERT.

risks_and_mitigations.risk: Tier 2 API calls add latency to phase transitions
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: Tier 2 only runs at two trigger points. claude-sonnet-4-20250514 with max_tokens=1024 responds in 2-3s. Phase transitions already involve container spawn/wait cycles of minutes.

risks_and_mitigations.risk: Tier 2 API failure blocks pipeline advancement
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: Wrap in try/except, return HEALTHY with warning on failure. Health check infrastructure failures never block the pipeline.

risks_and_mitigations.risk: False positives from Tier 2 cause premature failures
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: Tier 2 returns ALERT by default, not FAIL_PIPELINE. Only Tier 1 programmatic checks can enforce pipeline failure. Tier 2 enforcement can be enabled once confidence grows.

risks_and_mitigations.risk: Race conditions between health runner and existing reconciliation
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: Health checks are read-only inspections. Only the caller (cli.py, multi_agent.py, routes/pipelines.py) acts on results. Existing optimistic locking handles writes.
PipelineHealthContext uses lazy properties. Git operations only execute when Tier 2 accesses them. Tier 1 checks never trigger these.

risks_and_mitigations.risk: New health_checks package increases code volume
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: ~10 new files is proportionate to the feature scope. Each file is focused and testable. The alternative — inline everything — would make routes/pipelines.py even more unwieldy.

alternatives_considered.approach: Spawn sandbox container for Tier 2 evaluation
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Container startup takes 30+ seconds. Creates recursive monitoring problem. Direct API calls are faster, cheaper, simpler.
Import-time side effects make testing harder. Explicit runner is more transparent and injectable.

alternatives_considered.approach: Rewrite existing reconciliation as HealthCheck from scratch
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: 23 passing tests and production-proven code. Adapter pattern gives the unified interface without rewrite risk.

alternatives_considered.approach: Binary PASS/FAIL result instead of three-valued status
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Many failures are ambiguous. DEGRADED allows graduated response: escalate to Tier 2 rather than immediately kill the pipeline.

task_breakdown.description: Create orchestrator/health_checks/ package with types.py (HealthCheck protocol, HealthResult dataclass, HealthStatus/Tier/Trigger/Action enums) and context.py (PipelineHealthContext with lazy property accessors for git_log, git_diff_stat, agent_outputs, contract).
acceptance_criteria: HealthCheck protocol defined with name, tier, triggers properties and check() method
HealthResult dataclass with check_name, tier, status, reason, action, details, timestamp
All enums defined: HealthStatus (HEALTHY/DEGRADED/FAILED), Tier (PROGRAMMATIC/AGENT), Trigger (STARTUP/RUNTIME_TICK/WAVE_COMPLETE/PHASE_COMPLETE/ON_DEMAND), Action (CONTINUE/FAIL_PIPELINE/ALERT)
PipelineHealthContext with lazy git_log, git_diff_stat, agent_outputs, contract properties
Unit tests for type construction and context lazy loading

task_breakdown.title: Implement HealthCheckRunner with trigger dispatch and event emission
task_breakdown.description: Create runner.py with HealthCheckRunner. Supports register(), run_checks(), run_tier1(), run_tier2(). Implements trigger-based dispatch: runs Tier 1 first, escalates to Tier 2 at WAVE_COMPLETE if DEGRADED, always runs both at PHASE_COMPLETE. Emits events through EventBus. Add new EventType values to events.py.
acceptance_criteria: Runner registers checks and dispatches by trigger type
Tier 1 runs before Tier 2 in all cases
WAVE_COMPLETE: Tier 2 only runs if any Tier 1 result is DEGRADED
PHASE_COMPLETE: Both tiers always run
Events emitted via EventBus for each check result
New EventType values: HEALTH_CHECK_STARTED, HEALTH_CHECK_COMPLETED, HEALTH_CHECK_DEGRADED, HEALTH_CHECK_FAILED
Unit tests for registration, dispatch, escalation, event emission

task_breakdown.title: Create adapter checks for existing mechanisms
task_breakdown.description: Create ContainerLivenessCheck and StartupStateCheck adapter classes that implement HealthCheck protocol by delegating to existing container_monitor and startup_reconciliation code. No modifications to existing files.
acceptance_criteria: ContainerLivenessCheck conforms to HealthCheck protocol
StartupStateCheck conforms to HealthCheck protocol
Both delegate to existing code without modifying it
Existing tests for container_monitor.py and startup_reconciliation.py still pass unchanged
New adapter tests verify correct HealthResult generation for various scenarios

task_breakdown.title: Implement phase output presence check
task_breakdown.description: New Tier 1 check verifying completed phases produced expected artifacts. Checks for commits on remote branch (git log), agent output files in .egg-state/agent-outputs/, and contract task completion status. Phase-specific expectations (implement needs commits, plan needs architect output, etc.).
acceptance_criteria: Implement phase: verifies commits exist on remote, agent output files present
Plan phase: verifies architect-output.json and task_planner-output.json exist
Refine phase: verifies refiner-output.json exists
Returns DEGRADED when agents report success but artifacts missing
Returns HEALTHY when all expected artifacts present
Returns FAILED when no artifacts produced despite successful agents
Unit tests with mocked git operations and file system

task_breakdown.title: Implement state consistency check
task_breakdown.description: New Tier 1 check cross-referencing orchestrator pipeline state against Docker container reality and contract state.
acceptance_criteria: Detects containers marked RUNNING in pipeline but missing from Docker
Detects agents marked COMPLETE but contract tasks still PENDING
Returns FAILED for major inconsistencies
Returns DEGRADED for minor drift
Unit tests with mocked Docker client and state store

task_breakdown.title: Implement Tier 2 agent inspector
task_breakdown.description: LLM-based semantic health evaluation. Assembles context from pipeline state, git operations, agent outputs, and contract. Calls Claude API (claude-sonnet-4-20250514) with structured prompt. Parses JSON response. Handles API failures gracefully.
acceptance_criteria: Assembles context from git log, git diff --stat, agent outputs, contract, issue
Calls Claude API with structured output prompt and max_tokens=1024
Parses JSON response into HealthResult with status, reasoning, findings
Handles API failures gracefully: returns HEALTHY with warning reason
Returns ALERT action (not FAIL_PIPELINE) for DEGRADED/FAILED findings
Context capped at ~4000 tokens by truncating diffs
Unit tests with mocked API responses covering healthy, degraded, failed, and API error scenarios

Add GET /api/v1/pipelines/{id}/health endpoint. Add HealthCheckResultModel to models.py.

constraints: Existing startup_reconciliation.py and container_monitor.py must remain functionally unchanged (23 combined tests must pass without modification)
Health checks must be read-only — they inspect state but never mutate pipeline state directly
Only the caller (cli.py, multi_agent.py, routes/pipelines.py) can act on HealthResult by mutating state
Tier 2 agent inspector must handle API failures gracefully (return HEALTHY, never block the pipeline)
Health check results must flow through existing EventBus/SSE for observability
State mutations must respect optimistic locking via state_store
Tier 2 uses claude-sonnet-4-20250514 for cost efficiency (~$0.02-0.10 per call)
PipelineHealthContext lazy properties must not execute expensive operations for Tier 1 checks that don't need them
Health check infrastructure failure must never block or crash the pipeline
dependencies: Pipeline model (orchestrator/models.py) — pipeline state, phases, containers, agents
StateStore (orchestrator/state_store.py) — pipeline persistence and optimistic locking
Contract models (shared/egg_contracts/models.py) — task statuses, review feedback
Anthropic Python SDK — Tier 2 Claude API calls
